import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Brightwater Rentals tracks every piece of rental equipment as a record: name,
category, status, purchase price. In Facet that record type is a **doctype**.
You declare it once, and Facet checks every write against your declaration.
The declaration holds the fields, the identifier, the owned children, the
actions, and the templates that name and find each document.

## When to use this

You add a doctype to a draft, or you rework an existing one. Design the
doctype until it holds, then publish. See
[Choose how you build](/build/model/) for the two places you can edit.

## Before you start

- **Edit rights.** You need the right to edit doctypes in the target domain.
  In the app, the editor role holds it for the domains you edit.
- **A domain to live in.** The domain must exist before Facet accepts a
  doctype in it.
- **A free action name.** Eight names are reserved for the [lifecycle hooks](/build/model/behaviour/scripts-and-guards/)
  Facet calls itself: `validate`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, `migrate`,
  `snapshot`, `history`, `rollback`. Your own actions cannot use them.

## Steps

<Tabs syncKey="build-mode">
<TabItem label="Builder">

1. Open the draft of your domain in the **Builder** and go to the
   **Doctypes** tab. Pick **New doctype**.
2. Fill the identity block: **Name** (CamelCase, for example `Item`),
   **Label** (what users see), **Icon**, and the **Display name** template
   that names each document.
3. Add one row per field: name, type, and the constraints the data needs.
4. Mark the doctype as an **Aggregate root**, or attach it to a parent with
   **Member of**.
5. Save. Facet validates the schema and compiles the script; issues appear on
   the **Check** tab.

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Files">

Create `doctypes/equipment.Item.yml` in the domain folder. This is the
Brightwater item doctype; its script and actions live in their own files and
get their own pages:

```yaml
content:
  icon: package
  color: "#0F766E"
  domain: equipment
  doctype: Item
  aggregate_root: true
  schema_version: 1
  display_name: "{{ name }}"
  search: "{{ name }} {{ serial_number }}"
  identifier:
    template: "EQ-{year}-####"
  fields:
    name:
      type: string
      title: Name
      required: true
      filters: [equality, text_search]
    category:
      type: reference
      title: Category
      doctype: equipment.Category
      required: true
      filters: [equality]
    status:
      type: enum
      title: Status
      default: available
      filters: [equality]
      values:
        - key: available
          label: Available
          color: "#15803d"
        - key: out
          label: Out
          color: "#b45309"
        - key: in_repair
          label: In repair
          color: "#b91c1c"
    purchase_price:
      type: money
      title: Purchase price
      currency: EUR
      precision: 2
      tags: [finance]
      filters: [comparison, currency]
    serial_number:
      type: string
      title: Serial number
      unique: true
      filters: [equality]
    notes:
      type: longtext
      title: Notes
  sidecars:
    comments:
      doctype: core.Comment
      column: target
meta:
  parent_id: equipment
```

The watcher applies the file on save. See
[The domain file layout](/build/model/in-files/domain-files/) for where each
file sits.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

### What each part does

| Part | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | The name the interface shows, for example `Item`. Falls back to the doctype name. |
| `icon` | A Lucide icon name in kebab-case, for example `package`. An unknown name falls back to a plain mark. |
| `display_name` | A Jinja2 template that names each document, for example `{{ name }}`. |
| `search` | A Jinja2 template for the search text. A root doctype must declare `display_name` or `search`; `search` defaults to the display name, so the label alone is enough. |
| `fields` | The data. See [Choose field types](/build/model/data/field-types/). |
| `identifier` | Readable reference numbers. See [Reference numbers and uniqueness](/build/model/data/identifiers-uniqueness/). |
| `children` | Owned parts. See [Parent and child documents](/build/model/relations/parent-child/). |
| `sidecars` | Comments and attachments panels. See [Add comments and attachments](/build/model/relations/comments-attachments/). |
| `actions` | Typed operations users run from the document page. See [Named actions](/build/model/behaviour/named-actions/). |
| `scopes` | Saved row filters an administrator can hand to roles. See [Write row rules for roles](/build/model/access/named-scopes/). |
| `schema_version` | The data-shape version. Raise it only when a change on a live domain needs one. |

### Root or child

A doctype is exactly one of two things:

| Kind | Declaration | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aggregate root | `aggregate_root: true` | The record users create and delete. It is the unit of locking and of access control. |
| Owned child | `aggregate_root: false` plus `member_of` | A part of a parent document. See [Parent and child documents](/build/model/relations/parent-child/). |

Field names use `lower_snake_case` or `camelCase`. Facet rejects other
spellings, and it rejects a field that is both `read_only` and `write_only`.

## How a write flows

Every write follows the same path: Facet validates the document, appends one
row to the change log, updates the current version of the document, and
publishes one event. Hooks, webhooks, and live updates react to that event.

{/* d2
*One write, four steps*
direction: down
writer: "App or user" {class: external}
log: "Change log" {class: store}
current: "Current version" {class: store}
bus: "Event bus" {class: store}
consumers: "Hooks, webhooks, live updates" {class: external}

writer -> log: validated write
log -> current
log -> bus
bus -> consumers
*/}

## Troubleshooting

### The create answers `422 Domain 'crm' does not exist`

Create the domain first. A doctype needs a live or draft domain to live in.

### The create answers `422` with a key name

A definition accepts only known keys, and every field entry checks its own
keys. The message names the key and its location. Most often a constraint is
misspelled, for example `reqired` instead of `required`.

### The icon does not show

The icon value must match a Lucide icon name in kebab-case. Facet falls back
to a plain mark when the name is unknown.

### Publish refuses the doctype with a label error

An aggregate root must be able to produce a label. Declare a `display_name`
template, or a `search` template. A child is reached through its parent, so
it is exempt.
